title: Usage insights: audit log export actions + enforce RBAC on insights endpoints
author: Kevin Osei
description:
Motivation: Usage Insights introduces an export flow (CSV/JSON) that can be used in finance/ops workflows. For compliance and enterprise readiness we need (1) export/download actions to be audit logged with sufficient context, and (2) strict RBAC/tenant isolation on the Insights read APIs and export job endpoints so that org/project boundaries are enforced consistently.

This PR adds: (A) audit logging events for report export creation and download, including actor + scoping + filters; (B) shared authorization helpers applied to insights endpoints (top routes, route detail, model breakdown, export create, export download); (C) tests covering cross-project leakage and permission-denied behavior; (D) a security review checklist embedded in the PR to make the auditability/least-privilege expectations explicit.

Scope/details: - New audit events: usage_insights.export.created and usage_insights.export.downloaded - Fields captured: actor_user_id, actor_email (when available), org_id, project_id, environment, region, deployment_mode, time_range_start/end, route_filter (if provided), model_filter (if provided), export_format, row_limit, job_id, report_id, request_id, ip, user_agent - Export filters are logged in a normalized form (sorted keys; redacted/hashed where appropriate). We intentionally do not log prompt content or any request payload beyond filter primitives.

RBAC: - Enforces that the caller has insights:read for the requested org/project scope; for export creation/download also requires insights:export - For project-scoped API calls, rejects mismatched org_id/project_id combinations and prevents cross-project access even for users with org-wide membership but without project membership - Uses existing policy bundle hooks (AuthZ service) instead of duplicating checks in each handler.

Notes: - Audit logging is best-effort and does not block the primary request on transient audit sink failure; however, export download will emit a structured warning and increments audit_write_failed_total for SRE visibility - Added integration tests that spin up two projects under the same org and verify that exports created in Project A cannot be listed/downloaded from Project B - Includes a follow-up TODO to align naming with the final Confluence audit event schema doc once that page is stamped (this PR matches the current draft shared by Security).

Rollout: Behind feature flag usage_insights_exports_enabled (export paths already gated) and guarded by server-side RBAC regardless of flag. Audit logs are emitted in all environments; in staging we keep retention at the lower default.

Security review checklist (completed in this PR): - [x] RBAC enforced on every insights API entry point (including export download) - [x] Org/project scoping validated server-side (no client trust) - [x] Audit events contain who/when/what (filters) + request_id for correlation - [x] No sensitive payloads logged (prompts, completions) - [x] Failure modes documented (audit sink unavailable) and monitored via metric - [x] Unit + integration tests cover denial cases and cross-project isolation

Refs: Linear ENG-8428 (RBAC), ENG-8425 (Export). Support context: SUP-18475 (customer asked if exports are audit logged).

conversation: Naomi Feldman (Security/RBAC product review): Can we confirm we log sufficient context to be useful for compliance evidence (who, when, filters, and scoping)? Also want to ensure we are not logging any user data beyond filters.

Kevin Osei (Author): Yes — events include actor identifiers, org_id/project_id, env/region/deployment mode, time window, and filter primitives (route/model). No prompts or completions are logged. I added explicit redaction/normalization in usage_insights_events.ts and a test asserting the payload has no 'prompt'/'messages' keys.

Marcus Lin (Security engineering reviewer): Two concerns: (1) best-effort audit logging is OK, but we need visibility when it fails; (2) download endpoint must be protected even if someone guesses a report_id.

Kevin Osei (Author): Addressed both: added audit_write_failed_total metric + structured warning with request_id; download now calls requireInsightsExport() and also verifies report.project_id matches the caller scope (not just existence). Added integration tests that create export in projA and attempt download from projB.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (RBAC/tenant isolation engineer): Please avoid duplicating org/project validation logic across routes. Can we centralize the scope parsing + mismatch rejection so we don't diverge?

Kevin Osei (Author): Done — added requireOrgProjectScope() in insights_permissions.ts and used it in all four handlers (top routes, route detail, export create, export download). Also standardized the Forbidden payload in errors/forbidden.ts.
Allison Grant (Observability/SRE reviewer): For the audit failure metric, can we ensure tags won't explode cardinality? Avoid tagging by route or model.
Kevin Osei (Author): Good catch — metrics are tagged only by event_name and result (ok|failed). No route/model tags. Added a comment in audit_metrics.ts to prevent future additions.
Chloe Martin (Engineering lead, console backend): CI looks green. One nit: error codes should match the API contract (FORBIDDEN vs NOT_FOUND).
Kevin Osei (Author): Updated: cross-project access now returns 403 FORBIDDEN consistently; 404 only for missing resources within the caller scope. Added a test to lock this behavior.
Naomi Feldman (Security/RBAC product review): Approved. Checklist items look complete and match what we need for enterprise security reviews.
Marcus Lin (Security engineering reviewer): Approved after changes. Please open a follow-up to confirm retention settings for audit events in private/VPC mode.
Kevin Osei (Author): Will do — follow-up in Linear to align with the retention/residency review (ENG-8434).
release_notes: Console backend: Export create/download actions for Usage Insights now generate auditable events and enforce explicit RBAC permissions on all insights endpoints.
